W3aieHjyNvw.summary: Blizzard's Timothy Ford explains in this 2017 GDC session how Overwatch uses an Entity Component System architecture for layered gameplay. He also covers its server-authoritative netcode with client-side prediction and how they keep the game responsive and fair.
W3aieHjyNvw.why: HN treats it as the best real-world AAA example of ECS and game netcode, and cites it constantly in discussions of data-oriented design.

WXuK6gekU1Y.summary: Feature-length documentary following DeepMind's AlphaGo program as it prepares for and plays the 2016 match against Go champion Lee Sedol. It covers the team, the games, and the emotional reaction of the Go world to an AI beating a top human.
WXuK6gekU1Y.why: HN commenters call it a moving, well-made human story about AI and Go that works for non-technical viewers and does not date.

WpkDN78P884.summary: Robert C. Martin's Ruby Midwest 2011 keynote argues that software architecture should express the application's intent rather than its framework. He covers separating entities, interactors and boundaries so the web, database and framework are details.
WpkDN78P884.why: Frequently recommended as an influential talk on decoupled, testable architecture, though some commenters push back on Martin's TDD advocacy.

WwslBPj8GgI.summary: Harvard physicist Eric Mazur explains how he realized his students were memorizing rather than understanding, and how he changed his teaching. He presents peer instruction and data showing improved student performance.
WwslBPj8GgI.why: Repeatedly recommended in education threads as the definitive talk on why lectures fail and what works better.

WUvTyaaNkzM.summary: The first video of 3Blue1Brown's Essence of Calculus series, which builds toward integrals, derivatives, and the fundamental theorem of calculus from a simple geometry question. It aims to make viewers feel they could have invented calculus themselves.
WUvTyaaNkzM.why: A staple recommendation for anyone learning math, praised for visual intuition that makes memorized formulas make sense.

WVDQEoe6ZWY.summary: Tom Scott writes a more honest VPN ad, with the sponsor's name redacted, and explains why the typical claims in VPN advertising are misleading. He notes the sponsor was not happy about it.
WVDQEoe6ZWY.why: The standard link when VPN marketing comes up, as a clear debunking of the scare tactics behind VPN ads.

Wpv-Qb-dB6g.summary: Mirabai Knight's PyCon 2013 talk on Plover, a free cross-platform stenography engine that lets people write at up to 240 WPM on ordinary hardware, including a demo of coding by steno.
Wpv-Qb-dB6g.why: HN's standard reference when typing speed, ergonomics, or alternative input comes up, for its live demo and the open-source steno ecosystem.

WFCvkkDSfIU.summary: Drew Berry shows scientifically accurate animations of molecular processes inside cells, such as DNA replication, at TEDxSydney.
WFCvkkDSfIU.why: HN recommends it for mind-blowing visuals that make cell biology tangible.

WZskjLq040I.summary: Tom Scott plays the Royal Game of Ur against British Museum curator Irving Finkel, who deciphered its rules from a cuneiform tablet. Finkel teaches the game and explains its history as the oldest playable board game.
WZskjLq040I.why: Recommended in threads on ancient games and cuneiform as a charming match with an enthusiastic expert.

Wp-WiNXH6hI.summary: Carl Sagan's December 1985 testimony to Congress on the greenhouse effect, about 15 minutes long. He lays out CO2 warming, the risk of runaway effects and the danger of continued coal burning.
Wp-WiNXH6hI.why: HN commenters use it as proof that the climate problem was clearly explained decades ago, and as a model of clear communication to a broad audience.

WIyTZDHuarQ.summary: Veritasium shows silicone oil droplets bouncing on a vibrating bath, a physical analogue of pilot wave theory that reproduces quantum-like behavior such as double-slit patterns.
WIyTZDHuarQ.why: HN recommends it as a short, intuitive introduction to the pilot wave (de Broglie-Bohm) interpretation of quantum mechanics.

WTYet-qf1jo.summary: An animated, profane rant critiquing Windows 8, especially its touch-first interface on desktop PCs. The author draws on a background in tech journalism to lay out the UX problems.
WTYet-qf1jo.why: Linked in Windows 8 threads as a funny but accurate summary of its usability problems.

WlT3UhC7NwQ.summary: Chase Adam, founder of the nonprofit Watsi, speaks at Startup School 2013 about building a nonprofit startup.
WlT3UhC7NwQ.why: HN recommends it as an excellent speech from Watsi's founder, especially on keeping a nonprofit aligned with the people it serves.

WxOp5mBY9IY.summary: Footage from the Macworld Boston 1997 keynote where Steve Jobs announces Apple's deal with Microsoft, with Bill Gates appearing on the big screen. The almost bankrupt Apple took Microsoft's investment, and the crowd reacted badly, including booing over Internet Explorer as the default browser.
WxOp5mBY9IY.why: HN returns to it as a legendary moment in tech history and as a precedent for strategic deals between rivals, such as in the Nokia and Microsoft story.

W1czBcnX1Ww.summary: Boston Dynamics' March 2008 video of BigDog, a four-legged robot, walking on ice and snow, climbing rubble and recovering from slips and kicks.
W1czBcnX1Ww.why: HN returns to it as the classic jaw-dropping demo of legged robots handling rough terrain, and as a historical marker for how long such robots have existed.

WDIkqP4JbkE.summary: Scott Meyers explains how CPU caches work and why they matter for performance, covering cache levels, access speeds, associativity, and effects in multithreaded code. The focus is C++ and cache-aware, data-oriented programming.
WDIkqP4JbkE.why: HN points to it as the go-to explanation of why memory layout beats pointer-chasing structures on real hardware.

WEDIj9JBTC8.summary: A Big Think talk in which hedge-fund manager William Ackman goes through the basics of finance and investing in under an hour. It is pitched as a crash course on the most important concepts.
WEDIj9JBTC8.why: HN recommends it to beginners as a quick, clear overview of finance and investing fundamentals.

WYPNjSoDrqw.summary: A Dartmouth-produced documentary on how professors John Kemeny and Tom Kurtz, with a group of undergraduates, invented the BASIC language. It covers the creation of BASIC and the early time-sharing environment at Dartmouth.
WYPNjSoDrqw.why: HN recommends it as the definitive documentary on BASIC's origins, and it resurfaces whenever BASIC or Kurtz comes up.

Wx_kugSemfY.summary: Andrew Huang explains the harmonic series, which he calls the foundation of almost all music. He builds the idea up step by step, with demonstrations of overtones and how harmonies derive from them.
Wx_kugSemfY.why: HN recommends it as a clear, short but in-depth explanation of harmonics and overtones, useful even for musicians.

W71BTkUbdqE.summary: Rachel Potvin describes the scale of Google's codebase and its custom monolithic source repository. She explains the reasons for the monorepo model, the tooling that makes it workable, and its tradeoffs.
W71BTkUbdqE.why: The go-to reference in monorepo and trunk-based development discussions, recommended as a firsthand account of how Google manages source control.

W4SxKWwFhA0.summary: In a long live-coding session, Andreas Kling works on making the Cookie Clicker game playable in the Ladybird browser from SerenityOS. He tracks down bugs in the browser engine and fixes them.
W4SxKWwFhA0.why: HN loves the Browser hacking series for its clear debugging method of reducing bugs to minimal reproductions, which people say influenced their own testing.

W88Sact1kws.summary: A short narrated video describing how reintroducing wolves to Yellowstone triggered a trophic cascade that changed wildlife, vegetation and even river courses. This is a remastered HD version of George Monbiot's viral piece.
W88Sact1kws.why: HN cites it as a compelling example of unforeseen ecosystem effects and rewilding.

WB2-2j9e4co.summary: Kirsten Dirksen visits architect Gary Chang's 32 square meter Hong Kong apartment, which he has redesigned over decades. Sliding walls and transformable furniture turn it into 24 different room configurations.
WB2-2j9e4co.why: Held up as the ultimate example of small-space design and a beautiful compact home.

WRdJCFEqFTU.summary: Joscha Bach's 32C3 talk applies computational theories of mind to questions of meaning, emotion, and love, asking how computation can explain irrational-seeming human experience.
WRdJCFEqFTU.why: Recommended as one of the best bridges between mind and computation, and as a sample of Bach's thinking on AI and philosophy.

WVTWCPoUt8w.summary: Linus Torvalds tells the story of Linux in a 2001 talk at the Computer History Museum, from writing code as a graduate student in Helsinki in the early 1990s to becoming an icon of open source. It covers the project's origins, its growth, and his views on licensing and kernel design.
WVTWCPoUt8w.why: HN points to it as the long first-person account of Linux history, including Linus on the GPL's role and on microkernels.

Wi_nFz1CJSI.summary: Peter Zeihan speaks at Iowa Swine Day 2022 on geopolitics, the end of globalization and agriculture. He argues that supply chains, energy and farm inputs are all about to be disrupted.
Wi_nFz1CJSI.why: Recommended for its bleak take on globalization, energy and food supply, though some commenters question how objective it is.

Wp7GAKLSGnI.summary: A roughly three-hour Computer History Museum oral history interview of Donald Knuth by Edward Feigenbaum, recorded in 2007. Knuth covers his family, music, early programming, his thesis, The Art of Computer Programming, and the detour into TeX and METAFONT.
Wp7GAKLSGnI.why: HN recommends it as a superb, personal long-form look at Knuth's life and work habits.

W6aKQ-eBFk0.summary: Gamers Nexus benchmarks the Ryzen 9 7950X in its BIOS Eco Mode presets (65W, 105W and stock 170W). It measures the performance cost against the power and heat savings.
W6aKQ-eBFk0.why: Cited as evidence that Eco Mode gives large power savings for a small performance loss on Zen 4.

WHj2GaPuEhY.summary: A 1997 Noam Chomsky talk at Northeastern University about the gap between free-market rhetoric and practice. He argues that business relies heavily on state intervention, and he discusses trade, NAFTA and labour versus capital mobility.
WHj2GaPuEhY.why: Linked repeatedly in threads on monopolies, protectionism, and subsidies, usually as a source for the argument that free markets are an ideology more than a reality.

WITLR_qSPXk.summary: Part one of an American Airlines training video presented by Captain Warren VanderBurgh on automation dependency. It grew out of a program on wake turbulence avoidance, and this restored version has the audio cleaned up.
WITLR_qSPXk.why: HN cites it as the famous lecture on over-reliance on automation and on when to drop to a lower level of automation, applicable well beyond aviation.

WMSBRk5WG58.summary: Day 21 of Casey Muratori's Handmade Hero, which covers loading game code dynamically from a DLL on Windows. He builds hot reloading of C game code from scratch in about an hour and a half.
WMSBRk5WG58.why: Recommended as a clear, from-scratch demonstration of how simple code hot-reloading is with plain OS facilities.

WNWYk4DdT_E.summary: Sandy Munro and Cory discuss how Tesla Model 3 and Model Y bodies in white have evolved over five years, including giga castings and lean design.
WNWYk4DdT_E.why: Cited as an expert's account of why gigacasting works and how Tesla manufacturing has changed.

WO2X3oZEJOA.summary: Rob Miles explains "glitch" tokens, odd strings in large language model vocabularies that make the model produce gibberish. He covers how they likely arise from tokenizer training data, such as Reddit usernames, that never appeared in the model's own training.
WO2X3oZEJOA.why: HN points to it as the accessible explanation of why glitch tokens exist whenever tokenizers or odd GPT behavior come up.

WU0gvPcc3jQ.summary: Epic's Unreal Engine 5 tech demo set in the Matrix universe, with Keanu Reeves and Carrie-Anne Moss. It moves from a cinematic to a playable car chase through a large detailed city, with a behind-the-scenes look at the rendering at the end.
WU0gvPcc3jQ.why: Cited as an impressive real-time rendering showcase, with Nanite and a huge photorealistic city, that rivals film CGI.

WijoL3Hy_Bw.summary: A KOMO News documentary about Seattle's homelessness, addiction and street crime. It examines the City Council's policies, shows conditions on the streets and the impact on local businesses, and explores possible solutions.
WijoL3Hy_Bw.why: HN commenters link it as an overview of Seattle's deterioration when discussing homelessness and crime in West Coast cities.

WjTrfoiB0MQ.summary: Andrei Alexandrescu's CppCon 2015 talk on handling exceptional control flow declaratively in C++. It uses scope guards with success and failure variants, built on std::uncaught_exceptions, to replace ad hoc RAII classes and rethrowing try/catch blocks.
WjTrfoiB0MQ.why: Pointed to in threads on defer, scope_exit and RAII as the clearest treatment of scope guards.

Wo2m3jaJixU.summary: A Linear engineer talks about scaling the company's sync engine, which keeps client data local and synchronized. It follows an earlier talk on the same system.
Wo2m3jaJixU.why: Recommended whenever local-first software, sync engines and CRDT alternatives come up, as a practical production account.

Wpzvaqypav8.summary: A John Oliver Last Week Tonight segment on America's crumbling infrastructure and why maintenance is neglected and underfunded. It mixes comedy with real examples such as aging bridges and dams.
Wpzvaqypav8.why: HN commenters link it when discussions turn to dam failures, bridge collapses, or the unglamorous work of maintenance.

WrxZ4AZPdOQ.summary: A short ShaderToy piece by Martijn Steinrucken (The Art of Code) that renders rain on a windshield during a night drive, with blurred bokeh lights. It is set to music.
WrxZ4AZPdOQ.why: Shared as a stunning shader demo, with praise for its clear explanations of how it works.

Ws4kbgfpKCw.summary: Nathan Kutz presents the spatio-temporal dynamics of rotating detonation rocket engines, including combustion fronts that behave like solitons. He shows a bifurcation analysis of a multiscale model that captures the main features.
Ws4kbgfpKCw.why: HN commenters recommend it for its fluid dynamics of detonation waves and its high-speed imaging of rotating pulses.

WvwiH1DOK1M.summary: The Plasticity creator explains what a geometry kernel is and compares commercial options C3D, ACIS, and Parasolid, describing his months of research and why he chose as he did.
WvwiH1DOK1M.why: Cited in CAD threads as a rare plain-spoken comparison of commercial geometry kernels and their limitations.

WxK11RsLqp4.summary: React Helsinki meetup recording featuring a talk on lessons with Apollo GraphQL and Linear co-founder Tuomas Artman on real-time sync for web apps. The sync talk explains Linear's local-first architecture.
WxK11RsLqp4.why: Cited as the explanation of how Linear's fast, locally synced UI works.

Wm2h0cbvsw8.summary: Dylan Beattie's parody of 'We Didn't Start the Fire' with lyrics made entirely of real software framework names, ending in the chorus about building yet another framework.
Wm2h0cbvsw8.why: Shared as a funny programming joke poking at the endless proliferation of web frameworks.

W07ZpEv9Sog.summary: A DEF CON 19 talk by datagram introducing tamper-evident devices. It reviews how seals and similar products are designed and shows that they are often easily defeated, drawing on the DEF CON tamper-evident contest.
W07ZpEv9Sog.why: HN points to it in threads about physical security and tamper-evident seals as an informative look at how easily they are bypassed.

W5yVGmfivAk.summary: Dr. John Campbell reviews studies on vitamin D and immunity, including research on respiratory infections, during the early COVID-19 period.
W5yVGmfivAk.why: Commenters point to Campbell's channel as a low-tech, content-dense source of pandemic updates and early discussion of vitamin D.

WA0wKeokWUU.summary: John Oliver's Last Week Tonight segment takes on Dr. Oz and the dietary supplement industry. It explains what is problematic about both, with a comedic wrap-up.
WA0wKeokWUU.why: Cited when discussing sensational health journalism and supplement industry misinformation.

WAwDvbIfkos.summary: A short clip of Richard Feynman explaining how a train stays on its tracks, through the conical shape of wheels and how it handles curves without differentials.
WAwDvbIfkos.why: HN links it as a great, surprising explanation whenever rail wheels, gauge or curves come up.

WE58YisgFeQ.summary: TechAltar's history of Philips, once Europe's largest tech company and a world leader in lighting, radio and physical media. It traces how the company sold off or spun out its businesses, until little remains but the licensed name.
WE58YisgFeQ.why: HN points to it when asked why many Philips-branded products aren't made by Philips, and for the company's decline.

WNFf7nMIGnE.summary: Lin-Manuel Miranda performs an early version of the Hamilton idea, then called "The Hamilton Mixtape", at the White House poetry and spoken word evening in May 2009. He is accompanied by Alex Lacamoire and the audience laughs along at the premise of a hip-hop song about Alexander Hamilton.
WNFf7nMIGnE.why: HN commenters cite it as the origin point of Hamilton, the clip that first showed the idea and drew a big audience reaction.

WOHPuY88Ry4.summary: Johnny Cash's live performance of A Boy Named Sue at San Quentin in 1969, a comic country song about a man named Sue seeking revenge on his father.
WOHPuY88Ry4.why: Mostly invoked as a reference or joke in threads about names, the .su domain or hardship, rather than recommended.

WOOw2yWMSfk.summary: Inventor Marc Griffin pitches his game Bulletball to the American Inventor judges. The clip shows a long, costly commitment to a game idea.
WOOw2yWMSfk.why: Mostly used as a cautionary tale about risking everything on a weak idea, with one commenter seeing it as a lesson in determination.

WfNBmZy1Yuc.summary: An American Airlines training video by Captain Warren VanderBurgh on control malfunctions and flight instrument anomalies. It discusses real incidents such as runaway trim and instrument failures and how crews should respond.
WfNBmZy1Yuc.why: Cited in aviation threads as a gripping primary-source account of incidents like stabilizer trim moving without the pilot's knowledge.

WkxSyv5R1sg.summary: A documentary about Vipassana meditation in India's Tihar Prison, led by Kiran Bedi, the prison's Inspector General. It follows inmates who went through the courses and the changes they describe.
WkxSyv5R1sg.why: Cited as evidence that meditation can work as prison reform.

WmId2ZP3h0c.summary: A 2019 BBC News report by John Sudworth, who was given rare access to the secure facilities in Xinjiang where more than a million Muslims are thought to be held. Authorities call them training schools, and the report examines what the visit reveals about the system and conditions inside.
WmId2ZP3h0c.why: HN cites it as a stage-managed press tour of the camps, useful for seeing what was shown and what was hidden.

W18Z3UnnS_0.summary: A short GRASP Lab (University of Pennsylvania) demo in which teams of quadrotors autonomously assemble tower-like cubic structures from modular parts. The drones are given the target structure and work out the assembly plan themselves.
W18Z3UnnS_0.why: HN uses it as a go-to example of drones and robotics doing construction work.

W7QZnwKqopo.summary: A short BBC Planet Earth clip from the Pole to Pole episode showing the courtship displays of birds of paradise.
W7QZnwKqopo.why: HN references it as a vivid illustration of sexual selection and as a metaphor for competitive display.

WGRnhBmHYN0.summary: A short clip posted on the Donald J Trump channel of Joe Biden saying his campaign built the most extensive and inclusive voter fraud organization in history, widely taken as a gaffe for voter protection.
WGRnhBmHYN0.why: Mentioned only in passing in political threads, mostly critically.

WJOjSQ0yv8U.summary: 8-Bit Show And Tell walks through the BASIC source code of the original Commodore 64 Sid Meier's Pirates!. It covers bugs, quirks and traces of abandoned features and scenarios left in the code.
WJOjSQ0yv8U.why: Pointed to as a walkthrough of the BASIC listing of a famous game partly written in BASIC.

WPc-VEqBPHI.summary: A short clip of the Simpsons episode in which Homer designs a car with absurd requirements, used here as a lesson in project requirements and scope.
WPc-VEqBPHI.why: Used purely as a joke reference to scope creep and feature-bloated design.

WSatPoD2W-o.summary: A short clip in which Carl Icahn tells the story of his first activist investment and of firing 12 floors of people, arguing activism need not be short term.
WSatPoD2W-o.why: Used as an anecdote in layoff and cost-cutting debates: the company supposedly never noticed what the fired staff had done.

WV9J6sxCs5k.summary: A subtitled upload of the leaked February 2014 phone call between US diplomat Victoria Nuland and Ambassador Geoffrey Pyatt discussing Ukraine's future government, including the profane remark about the EU.
WV9J6sxCs5k.why: Not recommended as viewing; it is cited in Ukraine and geopolitics arguments as evidence of alleged US involvement in Ukraine's government.

WWKG6ZmgAX4.summary: A short clip of Barack Obama at the 2010 White House Correspondents Dinner joking that the Jonas Brothers should fear predator drones. It is posted by Michael Moore's channel with commentary on civilian drone deaths.
WWKG6ZmgAX4.why: Cited as an example of a joke about violence that could be stripped of context, or as a comparison when other politicians' jokes are criticized.

WY6KkRsS26M.summary: A short German satirical clip from Jung & Naiv at 32C3 mocking the German government's overuse of the word 'cyber'. It mixes press conference footage with jokes.
WY6KkRsS26M.why: Used as a joke or reference whenever politicians' 'cyber' buzzword comes up.

W_tqQYmgMQg.summary: A 1967 current-affairs segment interviews habitual drunk drivers just before the UK introduced the breathalyser. They insist they drive fine after drinking.
W_tqQYmgMQg.why: Used as a historical analogy for public resistance to new safety rules, and as an amusing vox pop.

WboggjN_G-4.summary: The People's Front of Judea scene from Monty Python's Life of Brian, a sketch about rival revolutionary groups.
WboggjN_G-4.why: HN people post it as a joke whenever factions that are nearly identical fight each other.

WiPp9YEBV0Q.summary: Kent Overstreet's Linux Foundation talk about writing a filesystem in Rust. Its Q&A segment, where Rust-for-Linux developers ask about interface semantics, became widely cited.
WiPp9YEBV0Q.why: Mostly cited as evidence of the friction between kernel maintainers and Rust developers, notably in Wedson Almeida Filho's resignation.

Wif1EAgEQKI.summary: Tom Scott's correction video on his earlier claim that 18th-century insurance firefighters let uninsured buildings burn. After a historian looked into it, he concludes the story was wrong and explains how the error happened.
Wif1EAgEQKI.why: HN mentions it as an example of a prominent creator publicly correcting a popular myth, and of the fire brigade myth itself.

WkZGL7RQBVw.summary: Declassified HUD footage of an F-16 whose unconscious pilot is saved by the Automatic Ground Collision Avoidance System. It shows the aircraft pulling out of a dive on its own.
WkZGL7RQBVw.why: Used as a concrete example of automation successfully saving an incapacitated pilot.

Wn190b4EJWk.summary: Rory McCune's AppSec EU 2015 talk on security risks in modern software deployment. It covers weaknesses in package ecosystems like npm, RubyGems and PyPI, and repository compromise.
Wn190b4EJWk.why: The speaker and others cite it in threads about malicious packages and typosquatting.

WpE_xMRiCLE.summary: A one-minute Robot Chicken stop-motion sketch where Darth Vader keeps altering his deal with Lando Calrissian.
WpE_xMRiCLE.why: Posted as a joke whenever someone changes the terms of an agreement after the fact.

Ws6AAhTw7RA.summary: A short demo from Tel-Aviv University of a superconductor locked in a magnetic field, hovering and staying fixed in place. It was shown at the 2011 ASTC conference.
Ws6AAhTw7RA.why: Linked in superconductivity and levitation threads as the canonical quantum locking demo.

WxyyJyB_Ssc.summary: Martin Odersky's JVM Language Summit 2015 talk argues that compilers can be thought of as databases. It describes design ideas for the Scala compiler and for developer tools.
WxyyJyB_Ssc.why: Cited as the origin of the compilers-as-databases idea in discussions of IDEs and incremental tooling.
